subject: Inference cost scoping and pilot rate calibration
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Morgan Lee <morgan@medix.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Inference cost scoping and pilot rate calibration

Hi Morgan — thanks for the chat earlier. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can size a clean pilot proposal:

- Notes from the call: Medix AI wants to run clinical summarization and triage pipelines (low-latency endpoints + async batch jobs). You expect a pilot to validate quality under production traffic patterns.

- Asks for pricing scoping: can you confirm (rough numbers are fine):
  1) Expected starting token volume per month for the pilot (avg/month).
  2) Peak daily token volume and typical request distribution (latency-sensitive vs batch).
  3) Target budget range or target $/1M tokens that would make a pilot viable.

I attached the usage export you shared over the call (Medix_MATP_Usage_Summary.csv) — I pulled a couple simple scenarios so we can map to unit pricing.

To help calibrate, our quick read from yesterday: OpenAI/Anthropic public list rates are a good baseline but actual cost varies a lot depending on batching, KV cache reuse, and model variant. If you can share the three numbers above we’ll send back a short bench table comparing expected per-1M token unit cost across: OpenAI hosted, Anthropic hosted, common open-model hosts, and a Redwood dedicated pilot estimate.

Proposed immediate next step: if you’re comfortable, send volumes/budget and we’ll return a 1-page pilot pricing comparison + SOW draft by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks —
Ben

Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Morgan Lee <morgan@medix.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Inference cost scoping and pilot rate calibration

Thanks Ben — appreciated the summary. Answers below: 

1) Pilot starting volume: ~40M tokens/month (customer-facing triage endpoints + internal QA).
2) Peak profile: spikes up to ~120-150M tokens/day on heavy load days (rare, ~1-2 days/month). Most traffic is latency-sensitive (65%) with the remainder batch inference (35%). Average prompt+completion length ~1.6k tokens.
3) Budget / target $/1M: We’d be comfortable evaluating anything in the ~$900–$1,600 per 1M tokens range for the pilot depending on SLA and data controls. Lower than that is obviously attractive, but procurement will need a clear committed consumption plan.

We'll also need visibility into (a) end-to-end latency (p95), (b) caching behavior on repeated patient prompts, and (c) data handling (audit logs/KMS).

Looping procurement in once we have a price and SOW they can review.

—Morgan
Morgan Lee
Head of ML Ops | Medix AI
morgan@medix.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Morgan Lee <morgan@medix.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 15:27:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Inference cost scoping and pilot rate calibration

Morgan — great, thanks for the numbers. Based on the volumes and latency split you shared, I put together a short benchmarking note comparing unit economics across common hosts and a Redwood pilot estimate. High level: 

- Assumptions we used: 1.6k tokens avg per request; 65/35 latency/batch; pilot commitment = 100M tokens/month for 3 months (we show sensitivity at 40M and 150M). 2) Model family: comparable open checkpoint (quant-friendly) vs Anthropic/Chat endpoint.

Benchmarks (approx $ per 1M tokens delivered, normalized):
- OpenAI hosted (baseline public rates + assumed hosting fees): $1,450 / 1M
- Anthropic hosted (public): $1,180 / 1M
- Common open-model host (managed open checkpoints, typical quantized runtime): $900–$1,100 / 1M
- Redwood pilot (dedicated pool + caching/batching optimizations): estimated $700–$950 / 1M depending on commit, model quantization, and KV cache hit rate

What explains the gap: open-hosts often use more conservative runtime settings (less batching, older kernels) and charge pump-on top for managed infra. Redwood’s number assumes: tuned kernels, adaptive batching for latency-sensitive traffic, prefix/KV cache reuse for triage flows, and the option to pin a quantized model. The tradeoff matrix: unit price vs latency SLO vs data isolation and SLA.

Pilot offer (draft):
- 3-month pilot, committed 100M tokens/month (flex +/- 30%).
- Pilot unit price: $900 / 1M (applies up to committed volume). Overages billed at $1,200 / 1M.
- SLA: 99.5% availability for inference endpoints, p95 latency target provided in the SOW appendix.
- Deliverables: onboarding playbook, latency dashboard access, audit logs, and a 1:1 tech review with our infra team during week 2.

I attached a short SOW draft and a pricing sheet (pilot-pricing-sheet.xlsx, Redwood-pilot-SOW-draft.pdf). If that pricing range looks reasonable I’ll have procurement-friendly language added and a redline-ready SOW by tomorrow.

Quick asks back to you: can procurement share their standard PO/T&Cs or should we propose Redwood standard terms with a mutual NDA + SOC 2 addendum?

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: Redwood-pilot-SOW-draft.pdf (pdf), pilot-pricing-sheet.xlsx (xlsx)

Looping procurement here so they can take the SOW/terms & route internally. Procurement — we’ll need a line on data handling, SOC 2 evidence, and a simple cancellation clause for the pilot. Ben — can you route the redline-ready SOW and the SOC 2 report link to procurement?

I’ll be available for a short kickoff next week if that helps.
